RagShortTexts: The Battle of Zama (202 BC) saw Scipio Africanus neutralize war elephants and defeat Hannibal with Numidian cavalry, ending the Second Punic War.

Variants.Content: In 204 BC, Scipio invaded North Africa, burning Punic camps and capturing Numidian king Syphax. Carthage desperately recalled Hannibal from Italy. On October 19, 202 BC, the titans clashed at Zama. Hannibal fielded 80 war elephants and 45,000 troops, while Scipio commanded 34,000 men reinforced by King Masinissa's premier Numidian cavalry. Anticipating elephant charges, Scipio arranged his maniples in parallel columns rather than the traditional checkerboard, opening clear lanes through which horn blasts channeled the beasts harmlessly. Masinissa's cavalry drove the Punic horse from the field, then struck Hannibal's veteran line from the rear, killing 20,000 Carthaginians. The Treaty of 201 BC stripped Carthage of Hispania, reduced its fleet to ten triremes, imposed a 10,000-talent indemnity, and forbade waging war without Roman consent.

At Zama, Publius Cornelius Scipio earned the immortal title Africanus! By opening lanes through his maniples, he made Hannibal's war elephants into harmless beasts, while Masinissa's riders hammered their rear. That glorious day avenged Cannae and crowned Rome the undisputed master of the Western world!

Zama was the twilight of our empire. Hannibal commanded raw conscripts alongside a depleted core of veterans, while Scipio wielded our former allies—Masinissa's Numidian cavalry. When those traitors charged our rear, seven hundred years of Punic sovereignty crashed down. We burned our proud ships and bent our knee to Roman dictates.
